minutes.headline: Select Board advanced the Food Pantry's temporary move to 30 School Street, waiving fees and OK'ing a license.
minutes.summary: The board presented three staff Merit Awards, publicly introduced new town manager Jessica "Jack" Miller, and voted to authorize a license agreement and waive building fees advancing the Lunenburg Food Pantry's temporary relocation to 30 School Street, amid public-comment dispute over whether that structure is "permanent" or "temporary." The board also referred zoning cleanup and stormwater-fee articles to the planning board for the November special town meeting, accepted a donated boulder for town hall, discussed but declined for now a MassWorks grant to study senior housing at the former TCP school, and debated (and largely declined) moving to a biweekly meeting schedule.

public_comment.stated_role: resident; chair of APDC and vice chair of the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee, speaking as a private citizen
public_comment.topic: Disputes the building commissioner's classification of the food pantry's proposed structure at 30 School Street as "permanent" rather than "temporary," and calls for a permanent town buildings/real estate planning committee.

Asks the board to refer Section 819 (2/3 vote for raising/appropriating money) to the Bylaw Review Committee so transfers require the same 2/3 threshold as appropriations at special town meeting, and criticizes the moderator's handling of a point of order at the September 3rd special town meeting.

Corrects earlier town-meeting figures on school extracurricular funding and, citing state end-of-year reports, argues the athletics fee schedule should be reevaluated so it again covers more of its own cost.

votes.motion: Approve the renewal of the earth removal permit at 780 Northfield Road.
Authorize the town manager to proceed with a license agreement with town counsel for the food pantry's temporary site.
Waive the building, wiring, plumbing, gas, sheet metal, and technology fees for the food pantry project.
Refer the special town meeting articles (zoning amendments and stormwater management bylaw fee structure) to the planning board for review and public hearing.
Accept the three donations (boulder, engraving, and installation work) for placement in front of town hall.
Approve the minutes of November 13, 2024, March 18, 2025, and April 22, 2025.
Approve the minutes of September 15, October 7, October 14, October 21, and November 17, 2025.

budget_items.what_was_said: The food pantry president said an amateur online estimate of applicable fees came to around this figure; the town manager listed building, wiring, plumbing, gas, sheet metal and technology fees as ones the select board could waive.
The town manager gave an off-the-cuff guess for the cost of a full reclamation of the potholed parking lot near the food pantry site, while the town looks into interim patching before winter.
Town and school staff are still reconciling FY26 close-out, including where the operating budget intersects with special revenue and grant funds, expected to finish in roughly two to three weeks.
Colonial Power was selected for a fixed-term supply contract; residents will get postcards about the new rate with a 30-day window to opt out before the November switchover.

A proposed special town meeting article would replace fixed dollar fee figures in the stormwater bylaw with a reference to the planning board's fee schedule as amended from time to time; referred to the planning board.

budget_items.topic: AED replacement using opioid settlement funds
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager proposed using the town's opioid settlement fund to replace AEDs, each costing roughly this amount with about a ten-year lifespan, across town and school buildings and police/fire vehicles.

budget_items.topic: TCP senior-housing feasibility grant proposal cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member cited a reported cost range to prepare a grant proposal exploring senior housing at the former TCP school, and argued the town could not fund that effort now.

The stormwater task force is preparing a non-binding article presenting two funding options -- a stormwater utility versus the operating budget -- for MS4 compliance, to go to the Finance Committee and a public info session before special town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Athletics spending and fee revenue share, FY2017 vs FY2025
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident, citing the state's end-of-year report, said athletics spending and the share covered by user fees changed sharply between fiscal 2017 and fiscal 2025.
The same resident said the dollar amount of athletics costs carried by taxpayers rather than fees rose over eight years.
The resident said general-fund transportation spending rose over four years as part of a broader cost trend he wanted the board to weigh.

budget_items.topic: Median household income of families with children in the schools
budget_items.what_was_said: The resident cited census data putting this group's median household income as the highest of any in town, as context for who bears extracurricular costs.

budget_items.topic: Tax-base share of extracurricular program costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The resident said most of the cost of extracurricular programs is carried by the broader tax base rather than by user fees.

budget_items.topic: Diesel fuel cost and school transportation budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member warned diesel prices approaching this figure could push transportation costs up again heading into next budget season.
A board member said a preliminary report indicated health insurance premiums could rise by about this percentage, cautioning the next budget season will likely be harder than last.

decisions.decision: The Brooks House long-term sale/lease report will be presented by subject-matter experts (planning, economic development and facilities staff) at the November special town meeting, closing out the November 2024 non-binding vote directive.

The boards/committees/commissions handbook review will be broken into roughly four rounds, with the first six chapters to be discussed at a future meeting in about two weeks; the remote-participation chapter will be handled separately.
The board will not pursue a MassWorks grant to study senior housing at the former TCP school this grant cycle, saying more public discussion is needed first.

Rather than adopt a strict every-other-week meeting schedule, the board will keep its default weekly Tuesday slot and cancel individual meetings as needed, with time-critical votes handled remotely if necessary.
The town manager will get PACC vendor quotes for audio/camera upgrades to the middle high school collaborative room, to evaluate it as an additional accessible meeting location.

what_happened.line: Select Board authorized a license agreement and waived building-department fees to advance the Food Pantry's move to 30 School Street.
A resident disputed the building commissioner's call that the new structure counts as permanent rather than temporary.
Board publicly introduced incoming town manager Jessica "Jack" Miller.
Zoning cleanup and a stormwater fee-bylaw article were referred to the planning board for the November 17 special town meeting.
Board declined to pursue a MassWorks grant this cycle to study senior housing at the former TCP school, citing a need for more public discussion.

why_it_matters: The food pantry's site status and its permanent-vs-temporary classification affect what oversight and process apply to future town-building decisions.
The stormwater bylaw change would tie fee amounts to a planning-board schedule that can change without a town meeting vote, which residents will be asked to weigh in November.
Passing on the MassWorks grant this cycle means no funded study of TCP senior housing for now, leaving that option undecided.
watch_next: November 17 special town meeting: zoning and stormwater fee articles, plus the Brooks House sale/lease report
FY26 budget close-out figures, expected in roughly two to three weeks

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The five non-procedural votes in our minutes match the official minutes in motion and outcome, all 5-0-0. The main difference is that the official minutes record two minutes-approval votes (4-0-1 and 3-0-2) that ours omit, and ours labels Jessica "Jak" Miller as town manager when the official makes her Assistant Town Manager.
